title: MARS-seq2.0: Experimental and Analytical Pipeline for Single-Cell RNA Sequencing
author: Hadas Keren Shaul
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.7hkhj4w

steps.title: Initialize Bravo Liquid-Handling Platform
steps.instruction: Turn on the Bravo liquid-handling platform, wait for initialization, and load the ‘cell capture plate preparation’ protocol file for the 96ST head.

steps.title: Prepare Cell Capture Plate Master Mixes
steps.instruction: Prepare lysis buffer (0.1% volume Triton X-100 in nuclease-free water) supplemented with 0.1 U/μl RNase inhibitor (RNasin Plus) and 1 mM RT1 primer for four barcode groups (Group 1: 1–96, Group 2: 97–192, Group 3: 193–288, Group 4: 289–384).

substeps.instruction: To prepare approximately twenty-four 384-well plates, use a multichannel pipette to mix 57.5 µL of lysis buffer with 5 µL of 12.5 nM RT1 primer stock per well of a 96-well plate.

steps.title: Dispense Master Mixes via Bravo Robot
steps.instruction: Place the 96-well master mix plates, filtered tips, and destination 384-well plates in the Bravo robot and run the preparation script.

substeps.instruction: The robot aspirates 2 µL from the group 1 master mix plate and dispenses it into destination 384-well plate 1, repeating for all desired plates.
Replace tips and repeat the process for groups 2, 3, and 4.
If more than three plates are prepared, replace filled destination plates when prompted.

steps.title: Store Cell Capture Plates
steps.instruction: Seal the prepared cell capture plates and freeze at -20 °C (stable for 1–2 years).

steps.title: Prepare for FACS Sorting
steps.instruction: Thaw cell capture plates from -20 °C, spin them down, and keep on ice until sorting.

substeps.instruction: Prepare a single-cell suspension for FACS; gate on SSC-A vs FSC-A for live cells and FSC-W vs FSC-A for singlets.
Calibrate the FACS machine for single-cell sorting into plates.

steps.title: Perform Single-Cell Sorting
steps.instruction: Place a cell capture plate in the FACS instrument and sort the desired population, leaving 2–4 empty wells per 384-well plate as no-cell controls.

substeps.instruction: Keep the single-cell suspension on ice until sorting.
Ensure the time from suspension to sorting does not exceed 4–5 hours.
Optional: Activate FACS Diva ‘index sorting’ function to record fluorescent marker levels.

steps.title: Post-Sorting Plate Processing
steps.instruction: Immediately after sorting each plate, seal with an aluminum sealer (must be low-temperature resistant), spin down to ensure cell immersion in lysis solution, snap-freeze on dry ice, and store at -80 °C.

steps.title: Sorting Efficiency Test (Optional)
steps.instruction: Test sorting efficiency using one or two plates from the session (not used for library prep).

substeps.instruction: Thaw one sorted 384-well plate for 5 minutes at room temperature and spin down.
Incubate the plate for 3 minutes at 72 °C to denature secondary structures, then immediately transfer to an ice block.
Add 2 µL of RT mix per reaction well to 2–4 columns per plate.
Seal, spin down, and incubate for 2 minutes at 42 °C, 50 minutes at 45 °C, and 5 minutes at 85 °C.
Spin down and dilute cDNA 1:20: (i) add 6 µL of EB8 to the RT columns to reach 10 µL; (ii) add 1 µL of this to 19 µL of EB8 in a separate plate.
Perform quantitative qPCR for mouse ActB or human GAPDH for 45 cycles.

steps.title: Automated RT Mix Addition
steps.instruction: Use the Bravo liquid handler to add RT reaction mix to the sorted 384-well plates.

substeps.instruction: Initialize Bravo and load the ‘RT mix addition’ script.
Thaw 384-well plates at room temperature for 5 minutes, spin down, and keep on ice.
Pre-heat a 384-well thermal cycler to 95 °C.
Prepare RT reaction mix and divide into two 8-well strips (16 µL per well) on a 4 °C 96-well CPAC unit.
Remove aluminum seal and place plate at 95 °C for 3–4 minutes for complete lysis buffer evaporation, then transfer to a 4 °C 384-well CPAC cooling block.
Run the script to add 0.5 µL of RT reaction mix to each well (final Triton X-100: 0.4% vol, RT primer: 4 nM).

steps.title: Reverse Transcription (RT) Program
steps.instruction: Seal the plate, spin down, and transfer to a 384-well thermal cycler for the RT program: 2 minutes at 42 °C, 50 minutes at 50 °C, and 5 minutes at 85 °C.

steps.title: Exonuclease I Treatment
steps.instruction: Use the Bravo robot to add Exonuclease I reaction mix to the RT-processed plates.

substeps.instruction: Spin down the 384-well plate and keep on ice; load ‘Exonuclease I addition’ Bravo script.
Prepare Exonuclease I mix and divide into two 8-well strips (32 µL per well) on a 4 °C 96-well CPAC unit.
Run the script to add 1 µL of Exonuclease I mix to each well in the 384-well plate (on 4 °C CPAC).
Seal, spin down, and incubate in a thermal cycler: 30 minutes at 37 °C and 10 minutes at 80 °C.

steps.title: Pooling of Single Cells
steps.instruction: Pool 384 single cells into amplification batches using the Bravo ‘Pooling’ script.

substeps.instruction: Prepare a 96-well pooling plate: dispense 55 µL of 0.1% volume Triton X-100 into each well of row H for tip pre-wash.
Spin down the 384-well plate and place in the robot.

Run the pooling script: tips are pre-washed, then contents of the 384-well plate are aspirated and dispensed into row A of the 96-well plate (12 wells, each containing 2 columns of the 384-well plate).
If multiple 384-well plates are used, pool subsequent plates into row B, C, etc.

steps.title: cDNA Purification and QC1
steps.instruction: Purify pooled cDNA using AMPure XP beads and perform initial quality control.

substeps.instruction: Spin down the 96-well pooling plate.
Add 86.4 µL of 0.9 volumes AMPure XP beads to each well, mix, and incubate for 5 minutes at room temperature.
Transfer contents of each row to a LoBind Eppendorf tube, complete AMPure XP cleanup, and elute in 19 µL of EB8.
Transfer 0.9 µL of pooled sample to 19.1 µL of EB8 for QC1 (qPCR of housekeeping gene).
Transfer 17 µL to the first column of a new 96-well plate.

steps.title: Second-Strand Synthesis
steps.instruction: Convert pooled cDNA to double-stranded DNA using a second-strand-synthesis kit (enzyme diluted 1:8 in nuclease-free water).

substeps.instruction: Mix the reaction well thoroughly with a 20-μl pipette.
Spin down and incubate at 16 °C for 2 hours.

steps.title: dsDNA Purification
steps.instruction: Purify the product using 1.4 volumes of AMPure XP beads.

substeps.instruction: Add 10 µL of EB8 and 42 µL of AMPure XP beads.
Complete cleanup and elute in 8 µL of EB8 (perform IVT directly with beads; do not transfer supernatant).

steps.title: In Vitro Transcription (IVT)
steps.instruction: Linearly amplify cDNA by adding 12 µL of IVT mix per well and incubating at 37 °C overnight.

steps.title: DNA Template Digestion
steps.instruction: Digest the DNA template by adding 10 µL of Turbo DNase I mix and incubating at 37 °C for 15 minutes.

steps.title: aRNA Purification
steps.instruction: Purify aRNA using 1.2 volumes of AMPure XP beads.

substeps.instruction: Add 20 µL of EB7.5 and 60 µL of AMPure XP beads.
Complete cleanup and elute with 19 µL of EB7.5.
Transfer 18 µL to a well in a new column of the 96-well plate, ensuring no beads are transferred.

steps.title: Chemical Fragmentation of aRNA
steps.instruction: Fragment aRNA to a median size of ~300 nucleotides using Zn2+ RNA fragmentation solution.

substeps.instruction: If aRNA was frozen, thaw on ice and spin down.
Add 2 µL of 10× Zn2+ fragmentation reagent to the aRNA.
Incubate for 3 minutes at 70 °C in a pre-heated thermal cycler.
Immediately transfer to a cooling block and add 2 µL of stop solution.
Cool for 1–2 minutes and spin down.

steps.title: Fragmented RNA Purification
steps.instruction: Purify fragmented RNA using 2 volumes of AMPure XP beads.

substeps.instruction: Add 44 µL of AMPure XP beads.
Complete cleanup (note: drying time is shorter than other steps).
Elute with 5.5 µL of EB7.5 and transfer 5 µL to a new column, ensuring no beads are transferred.

steps.title: Plate Adaptor Ligation
steps.instruction: Ligate a unique plate adaptor to the fragmented RNA.

substeps.instruction: Add 1 µL of 100 µM ligation plate adaptor and incubate for 3 minutes at 70 °C in a pre-heated thermal cycler, then transfer immediately to a cooling block.
Prepare ligation master mix in a LoBind tube (vortex/spin after each reagent; DMSO and PEG at 37 °C; store ATP at -80 °C).
Add 14.1 µL of ligation mix to the aRNA/adaptor mixture, mix slowly, and spin down.
Incubate at 22 °C for 2 hours.

steps.title: Ligation Product Purification
steps.instruction: Purify the ligation product using 1.5 volumes of AMPure XP beads.

substeps.instruction: Add 80 µL of EB7.5 and 100 µL of AMPure XP beads.
Complete cleanup (note: magnetization and drying times are longer, 7–8 min).
Elute with 13.7 µL of EB7.5 and transfer 13.2 µL to a new column.

steps.title: Second Reverse Transcription (RT2)
steps.instruction: Reverse-transcribe the ligated product using a primer complementary to the adaptor.

substeps.instruction: Add 1 µL of 25 µM RT2 primer to the purified ligated aRNA, mix by pipetting, seal, and spin down (total volume 14.2 µL).
Prepare RT mix and add 5.8 µL per reaction well.
Seal, spin down, and incubate: 2 minutes at 42 °C, 50 minutes at 45 °C, and 5 minutes at 85 °C.

steps.title: cDNA Purification and QC2
steps.instruction: Purify the resulting cDNA using 1.5 volumes of AMPure XP beads.

substeps.instruction: Add 10 µL of EB8 and 45 µL of AMPure XP beads.
Complete cleanup and elute in 25 µL of EB8.
Transfer 24 µL to a new column.
Take 1.2 µL of cDNA and add to 18.8 µL of EB8 for QC2.

steps.title: Library Amplification via PCR
steps.instruction: Amplify the cDNA to complete the library.

substeps.instruction: Transfer 11.5 µL of cDNA to a new column and add 12.5 µL of KAPA HiFi HotStart ReadyMix and 1 µL of 25 µM enrichment primer mix.
Run PCR (typically 11–17 cycles; example: 2 cycles at 57 °C and 12 cycles at 65 °C annealing temperature).

steps.title: Final Library Purification and QC3
steps.instruction: Purify the amplified library using 0.7 volumes of AMPure XP beads.

substeps.instruction: Add 35 µL of EB8 and 42 µL of AMPure XP beads.
Complete cleanup and elute with 20 µL of EB8.
Transfer 19 µL of the final library to a new well.
Take 2 µL of the final library and add to 38 µL of EB8 for QC3.

steps.title: Library Quality Assessment
steps.instruction: Measure concentration and evaluate the library profile.

substeps.instruction: Measure concentration (ng/μl) using dsDNA HS Assay Kit and Qubit fluorometer (use 2 µL for accuracy). Typical yield: 1–10 ng/μl.
Evaluate profile and mean molecule size using a 2200 TapeStation or equivalent.

steps.title: Library Pooling and Sequencing
steps.instruction: Calculate molarity, dilute, and sequence the libraries.

substeps.instruction: Calculate molarity using Qubit concentration and TapeStation peak size.
Dilute each pool to 4 nM with EB8 and mix pools in equal ratios.
Sequence (e.g., NextSeq 500 High Output v2 kit) with parameters: rd1 = 75 bp, rd2 = 15 bp, no indices.

steps.title: Analytical Pipeline Processing
steps.instruction: Process raw reads using the MARS-seq2.0 analytical pipeline.

substeps.instruction: Ensure correct SCDB directory structure in Linux storage.
Verify parameters in scdb/config/config.txt.
Add metadata to the sequenced library according to SCDB.
Add .fastq files to the SCDB.
Run the pipeline locally or on an SGE cluster.
